title: Dayanand Social Security Scheme Goa - Monthly Pension
meta_description: Dayanand Social Security Scheme Goa gives monthly pension to elderly, disabled, and widows. Check eligibility, pension amount, income limit, and how to apply.

hero.one_liner: Dayanand Social Security Scheme is Goa's main social pension. Old age pension is Rs 2,000 a month for those 60+, with other categories from Rs 1,500.

what_is_it: The Dayanand Social Security Scheme (DSSS) is Goa's primary social pension programme administered by the Social Security Department, providing a monthly pension of Rs 2,000 to elderly persons aged 60 and above, widows, persons with disabilities, and destitute women who have no other source of regular income; the scheme is named after Dayanand Bandodkar, Goa's first Chief Minister, reflecting the state's tradition of honouring its leaders through welfare policy. Payment is made directly to beneficiaries' individual bank accounts through Direct Benefit Transfer, ensuring reliable and transparent delivery without the need for the beneficiary to visit a government office or bank branch for each payment.

The old age pension category under DSSS is available to Goa residents aged 60 years and above whose family income from all sources is below Rs 3 lakh per year; there is no requirement that the applicant be below the poverty line, which makes the scheme relatively inclusive compared to central government social pension programmes that typically target only BPL households. The 15-year residency requirement ensures that only long-term Goa residents benefit, and the residency certificate must be issued by the local Panchayat or Municipal Council.

eligibility_filters.notes: Goa residents who are senior citizens (60+), single women, or persons with disabilities, family income below Rs 3 lakh a year. Old age pension Rs 2,000 a month, other categories Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,500, by DBT. Yearly life and income certificate required, or pension stops. Withdraw within six months to avoid reversal. Run by Directorate of Social Welfare.

how_to_apply.title: Collect Documents
how_to_apply.description: Gather your Aadhaar card, residency certificate (15 years in Goa from Panchayat or Municipal Council), income certificate below Rs 3 lakh/year, age proof or widow's husband's death certificate or disability certificate (as applicable), bank passbook, and two passport-size photographs.

how_to_apply.title: Submit Application at BDO or Municipal Office
how_to_apply.description: Visit the Block Development Officer's office (rural) or Municipal Council social welfare desk (urban), collect the DSSS application form, fill it in, attach all documents, and submit; an acknowledgment is issued upon receipt.

how_to_apply.title: Verification and Approval
how_to_apply.description: The BDO or municipal office verifies documents and forwards the eligible application to the Social Security Department for final approval; the department cross-checks the application against the existing beneficiary database before adding the applicant to the pension roll.

how_to_apply.title: Monthly DBT Payment
how_to_apply.description: Once approved, Rs 2,000 is credited to your bank account every month through Direct Benefit Transfer; ensure your Aadhaar is linked to your bank account for uninterrupted payment, and submit the annual life certificate when required.

extra_sections.heading: Understanding Dayanand Social Security Scheme
content: The widow pension under DSSS is available to women aged 18 years and above who have been widowed and whose family income is below Rs 3 lakh per year; unlike the old age pension, there is no minimum age requirement for widows, recognising that widowhood can occur at any age and that young widows who lose their primary breadwinner are among the most economically vulnerable members of society. The scheme's inclusion of all widows irrespective of age is a significant feature that sets Goa apart from states that restrict widow pensions to women above 40 or 50 years of age.

Persons with disabilities of 40 percent or more are eligible for the disability pension under DSSS, provided they meet the income and residency conditions; the 40 percent disability threshold is consistent with the Persons with Disabilities Act's definition of significant disability, and the disability must be certified by a Medical Board or Competent Medical Authority designated by the Goa government. The disability certificate is a mandatory document for this category of applicants and must specify the nature and percentage of disability.

extra_sections.heading: Understanding Dayanand Social Security Scheme: Going Deeper
content: The destitute women category under DSSS covers women who are not widowed, elderly, or disabled but are without any means of support due to abandonment, separation, or other social circumstances; this category reflects Goa's recognition that vulnerability among women is not always captured by the standard pension categories and that some women require social protection even if they do not fit neatly into widow or old-age classifications. Destitute women applicants must provide documentation of their situation, typically a declaration or certification from the local Panchayat.

The monthly pension of Rs 2,000 under DSSS is notably higher than the pension amounts provided under the central government's NSAP (National Social Assistance Programme) component schemes, which provide only Rs 200 to Rs 500 per month; Goa tops up the central NSAP amount for BPL beneficiaries to reach the Rs 2,000 state pension level, ensuring that NSAP-enrolled beneficiaries in Goa receive the same total monthly amount as other DSSS pensioners regardless of their BPL status. This convergence of central and state pension schemes is administered by the Social Security Department.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: Applications for DSSS are submitted at the office of the Block Development Officer (BDO) for rural areas or the Municipal Council's social welfare desk for urban areas; applicants must bring Aadhaar card, age proof (for old age pension), death certificate of husband (for widow pension), disability certificate from a Competent Medical Authority (for disability pension), residency certificate from the Panchayat or Municipal Council, income certificate from a Competent Authority, and two recent passport-size photographs. The BDO office or municipal desk issues an acknowledgment upon receipt of the application.

After verification by the BDO or municipal office, eligible applications are forwarded to the Social Security Department for final approval and inclusion on the pension roll; the department's scrutiny includes cross-referencing the applicant's details with existing pension beneficiary databases to ensure there is no duplication. New beneficiaries are added to the monthly DBT cycle from the date of approval, and the pension is credited to the beneficiary's individual bank account on a fixed date each month.

extra_sections.title: Goa's Main Social Pension
extra_sections.content:
The Dayanand Social Security Scheme is Goa's main social pension, paying a monthly amount to the most vulnerable. Old age pension is Rs 2,000 a month for those 60 and above.

It covers senior citizens, single women, persons with disabilities, and other vulnerable groups, for families with income below Rs 3 lakh a year.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible: Further Notes
content: The income limit of Rs 3 lakh per year under DSSS reflects Goa's higher cost of living and economic profile; in most other Indian states, social pensions are restricted to households below the BPL line or with income below Rs 1 lakh per year. Goa's higher income ceiling means that a larger proportion of the state's elderly, widowed, and disabled population qualifies for DSSS, making the scheme one of the more inclusive social pension programmes in India in terms of income coverage.

The Social Security Department in Goa conducts periodic reviews of the DSSS beneficiary list to verify continued eligibility; beneficiaries who cross the income limit, change their residency status, or whose circumstances change (for example, a widow who remarries) are removed from the pension roll after due verification. Beneficiaries are required to submit a life certificate each year to confirm that they are alive and their eligibility conditions have not changed; failure to submit the life certificate can result in suspension of the pension.

extra_sections.heading: What the Rules Say
content: The Rs 2,000 monthly pension is automatically revised upward when the state government decides to increase the amount; past revisions have progressively raised the pension from lower historical levels, and existing beneficiaries benefit from any upward revision from the effective date of the increase without needing to submit a fresh application. The government has committed to periodically reviewing the pension amount to ensure it keeps pace with the cost of living in Goa.

Beneficiaries of DSSS who also have disabilities qualifying them for central government schemes such as the IGNWPS or IGNOAPS under NSAP receive a consolidated pension that includes both the central component and the Goa state top-up; the Social Security Department coordinates with the centre to ensure seamless payment of the consolidated amount through a single DBT transaction to the beneficiary's bank account. This single-window payment reduces confusion and administrative burden for beneficiaries.

extra_sections.heading: What the Rules Say: The Specifics
content: Goa's Social Security Department also facilitates awareness of DSSS through Anganwadi workers, ASHA workers, and Gram Sabha meetings in rural Panchayat areas; in urban areas, awareness is spread through Municipal Council outreach and community notice boards. The department's field staff are trained to identify potential DSSS beneficiaries during their routine community visits and to assist them with the application process.

The Dayanand Social Security Scheme is part of a broader social protection architecture in Goa that also includes the Griha Aadhar Scheme for homemakers, the Ladli Laxmi scheme for girl children, and housing assistance programmes; together these schemes form a safety net that covers a wide range of vulnerable and economically marginal population groups in Goa. The convergence of these programmes is coordinated by the Social Security and Women and Child Development departments to ensure comprehensive coverage.

extra_sections.title: Different Amounts by Category
extra_sections.desc:
The pension is not a single flat amount. Old age pension is Rs 2,000, while other categories range from Rs 1,500 to Rs 2,500 a month.

The amount depends on the group you fall in, such as senior citizen, single woman, or a special vulnerable category.

extra_sections.heading: The Application Process
content: Pensioners under DSSS who are too old or infirm to visit the bank to collect their pension receive their payments directly in their bank accounts through DBT, eliminating the need for physical collection; pensioners with Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts also benefit from bio-authentication that can be done at their doorstep through micro-ATMs or Business Correspondents, particularly in rural areas with limited bank branch access. The Goa government has worked with banks to ensure that Business Correspondent networks cover remote areas of the state.

Goa's DSSS has been recognised as one of the more generous state social pension programmes in India in terms of both the monthly amount and the income ceiling; the scheme's design choices reflect the state's relatively higher fiscal capacity, its higher cost of living, and its political tradition of using welfare spending as a means of directly improving the quality of life of vulnerable citizens. The named association with Dayanand Bandodkar also gives the scheme a symbolic significance that reinforces its place in Goa's welfare identity.

extra_sections.heading: The Application Process: Further Notes
content: Eligible residents of Goa who have not yet applied for DSSS are encouraged to do so as early as possible, since the pension is paid from the date of approval rather than retroactively from the date of eligibility; many eligible elderly and disabled persons who are unaware of the scheme miss out on years of pension entitlement. The Social Security Department's helpdesk and the local BDO office can assist applicants in filling the form and gathering the required documents.

The DSSS framework also includes a provision for reassessment of pension amounts for persons with progressive disabilities; if a beneficiary's disability worsens over time and reaches a higher percentage on reassessment by the Medical Board, the department updates the beneficiary's record accordingly, and the updated disability certificate replaces the earlier one in the department's database. Beneficiaries whose disability level changes are advised to seek a fresh assessment from the Medical Board and submit the updated certificate to their BDO office.

extra_sections.title: File Your Yearly Certificates
extra_sections.content:
The pension needs a yearly life certificate and income certificate. If you miss them, the pension stops.

Once you submit them, the pension resumes from the next month, so file them on time to avoid a gap.

extra_sections.heading: How the Payment Reaches You
content: The Social Security Department in Goa maintains an online beneficiary portal where DSSS pensioners can check the status of their monthly payment, update their bank account details, and download receipts for the pension credits; this digital transparency reduces the need for pensioners to visit the department office for routine queries and allows them to resolve payment discrepancies quickly by raising an online grievance. The portal is accessible via the Goa government's official website.

DSSS pensioners in Goa who are also eligible for the Griha Aadhar Scheme can receive both benefits simultaneously if they meet the eligibility conditions for each scheme independently; for example, a widowed woman below 60 years who is a homemaker and meets the income and residency conditions may receive both the widow pension under DSSS and the homemaker assistance under Griha Aadhar. The two schemes are designed to be complementary rather than mutually exclusive, provided the applicant genuinely meets all eligibility conditions for each.

extra_sections.heading: How the Payment Reaches You: More Detail
content: Goa's Social Security Department also runs special camps in remote areas of the state to enrol eligible DSSS applicants who find it difficult to travel to the BDO office; these camps, held in coordination with the local Panchayat, allow applicants to complete document verification and submit their application on the spot. The camp-based enrolment model has been particularly effective in reaching elderly and disabled applicants in Goa's interior talukas who would otherwise face significant barriers to accessing the scheme.

The DSSS pension, combined with Goa's universal health insurance scheme and other state welfare programmes, forms a social protection floor for Goa's most vulnerable citizens that is more comprehensive than what is available in most other Indian states; for an elderly person receiving Rs 2,000/month from DSSS plus health coverage under a state health insurance scheme, the combined support represents a meaningful safety net that allows them to meet basic needs without being entirely dependent on family members. This comprehensiveness of Goa's welfare architecture is a reflection of the state's relatively higher fiscal capacity and political commitment to welfare.

extra_sections.title: Do Not Let It Accumulate
extra_sections.content:
As with other Goa welfare schemes, leaving the money unwithdrawn for six months or more can lead to a reversal.

Withdraw regularly, and keep your bank and Aadhaar link active so the pension keeps coming.

extra_sections.heading: The Paperwork
content: Applicants who are uncertain whether they qualify for DSSS or which category they fall under are advised to visit the nearest BDO office and speak with the social welfare officer, who can review their circumstances and advise on eligibility; the BDO office is the primary point of contact for all DSSS-related queries, and the staff are trained to guide applicants through the categorisation and documentation process. The department also has a toll-free helpline for DSSS queries that can be accessed from anywhere in Goa.

For elderly DSSS pensioners who are hospitalised or bedridden and cannot submit the annual life certificate in person, the Social Security Department accepts certificates countersigned by a gazetted officer, doctor, or the local Panchayat president; this accommodation ensures that the most vulnerable beneficiaries are not penalised due to physical inability to attend in person. Caregivers of bedridden elderly beneficiaries are advised to contact their BDO office to understand the exact procedure for submitting the life certificate on behalf of the pensioner.

extra_sections.title: The Paperwork Notes
extra_sections.content:
The Goa government has also integrated DSSS with the state's food security schemes; BPL beneficiaries who receive DSSS pension are automatically enrolled in the priority household category under the National Food Security Act, giving them access to subsidised ration at Rs 2 per kg for wheat and Rs 3 per kg for rice through the Public Distribution System. This inter-scheme convergence ensures that the poorest DSSS beneficiaries receive both income support and food security simultaneously.

Women beneficiaries of DSSS who are members of Self Help Groups (SHGs) can leverage their regular pension credit as proof of income for accessing micro-finance loans through SHG-linked credit programmes; banks that operate SHG lending programmes in Goa accept the DBT credit history of DSSS pensioners as evidence of a regular income stream. This has enabled some DSSS widow and elderly pensioners to access small loans for productive activities or emergencies without needing a guarantor.

extra_sections.heading: When Something Goes Wrong
content: The DSSS pension is not treated as taxable income and does not affect the beneficiary's eligibility for other government subsidies and entitlements that are means-tested based on family income; the Rs 2,000 monthly pension is specifically excluded from the income calculation for purposes of determining eligibility for the Goa government's other welfare schemes. This exclusion ensures that DSSS pensioners who receive other state welfare benefits do not become ineligible for those benefits because of the DSSS pension amount.

Goa's Social Security Department publishes an annual report on DSSS that includes data on the number of active beneficiaries, category-wise distribution, and the total amount disbursed; this transparency in welfare reporting allows civil society organisations and researchers to track the reach and financial impact of the scheme. The annual report is available on the department's website and at the district BDO offices for public reference.

Persons who have recently moved to Goa from another state and are approaching the 15-year residency mark are advised to begin collecting residency documentation as soon as they arrive, since proving continuous residency over 15 years requires documents spanning that entire period; electricity bills, ration cards, Panchayat voter roll entries, and children's school admission records from the relevant years are all accepted as supporting residency evidence. Applicants who can demonstrate continuous residency through a combination of such documents alongside the Panchayat residency certificate are more likely to have their applications approved without objection.

extra_sections.title: In Their Words Notes
extra_sections.content: With a monthly pension of Rs 2,000 for elderly, widows, and disabled persons and an income ceiling of Rs 3 lakh, the Dayanand Social Security Scheme is one of India's most inclusive state social pension programmes, reaching far beyond the BPL population to support Goa's economically vulnerable citizens.

faqs.question: What is the Dayanand Social Security Scheme?
faqs.answer: DSSS is Goa's main social pension scheme providing Rs 2,000 per month to elderly persons (60+), widows (18+), persons with 40%+ disability, and destitute women who are long-term Goa residents with family income below Rs 3 lakh/year.

faqs.question: How much pension is provided under DSSS?
faqs.answer: Rs 2,000 per month for all categories - old age, widow, disability, and destitute women.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the old age pension under DSSS?
faqs.answer: Goa residents aged 60 years and above with family income below Rs 3 lakh/year and at least 15 years of Goa residency, who are not receiving any other monthly state pension.

faqs.question: What is the age requirement for the widow pension under DSSS?
faqs.answer: There is no minimum age - widows aged 18 years and above who meet the income and residency conditions are eligible.

faqs.question: What disability percentage is required for the disability pension?
faqs.answer: 40 percent or more disability, certified by a Competent Medical Authority or Medical Board designated by the Goa government.

faqs.question: What is the income limit for DSSS?
faqs.answer: Family income from all sources must be below Rs 3 lakh per year. This is a relatively high ceiling that makes the scheme more inclusive than most state pension programmes in India.

faqs.question: What is the residency requirement for DSSS?
faqs.answer: The applicant must have resided in Goa for at least 15 consecutive years, verified through a certificate from the Gram Panchayat or Municipal Council.

faqs.question: Where do I apply for DSSS?
faqs.answer: At the Block Development Officer's office for rural applicants, or the Municipal Council's social welfare desk for urban applicants. Bring Aadhaar, residency certificate, income certificate, and the relevant category document (death certificate, disability certificate, or age proof).

faqs.question: Do I need to submit a life certificate every year?
faqs.answer:
Yes. DSSS pensioners are required to submit an annual life certificate to confirm continued eligibility.

Failure to submit can result in suspension of the monthly pension.

faqs.question: Is the DSSS pension paid through DBT?
faqs.answer: Yes. Rs 2,000 is credited directly to the beneficiary's individual bank account through Direct Benefit Transfer every month.
